chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, who said:

The fasting person in the month of Ramadan may use the miswak whenever he wishes. And if he rinses his mouth (madmadah) during the time of an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, there is no penalty upon him and his fast is complete. But if he rinses his mouth during a time other than an obligatory prayer and water enters his throat, he must repeat the fast. And it is preferable for the fasting person not to rinse his mouth.
ai.seo_question: Does rinsing the mouth break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the juristic distinction between the time of obligatory prayer (waqt al-faridah) and other times regarding the validity of the fast when water enters the throat during rinsing. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that accidental ingestion during the specific ritual context of prayer does not invalidate the fast, whereas it does at other times, while recommending caution (istihbab) to avoid rinsing entirely to preserve the fast's integrity.
